explanation: For each distinct keyword, track the latest possible starting index of a prefix of the required sequence. A matching later keyword extends the preceding prefix. Whenever the final keyword matches, compare the resulting interval with the best seen.
timeComplexity: O(n + k) expected time for n paragraph entries and k distinct keywords. Each paragraph word updates at most one state after O(k) keyword indexing. The entry-count bound treats word hashing/comparison as constant; include examined character lengths when words are unbounded.
spaceComplexity: O(k) auxiliary space. There are O(k) keyword indices and prefix states.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: For each keyword position j, start[j] stores the latest starting position of a valid sequence of keywords 0 through j in the processed paragraph. The first keyword starts a new prefix; a later keyword can extend only a previously completed preceding prefix. Keeping the latest start minimizes the length for any fixed ending position. Checking every occurrence of the final keyword therefore finds a globally shortest covering interval.
walkthrough: Use paragraph [elm, oak, cedar, elm, oak, ash, pine] and ordered keywords [elm, oak, ash]. The first elm/oak prefix starts at 0. The elm at index 3 replaces its start, and oak at 4 extends that newer prefix. Ash at 5 completes indices [3, 5], a three-word interval. The method returns (3, 5); the existing judge reports its length, 3. The callable returns inclusive zero-based endpoints. The executable walkthrough expected value is their length after the wrapper checks the required keyword sequence.
edgeCases: Keywords are distinct and the supplied corpus guarantees a covering interval.
Repeated paragraph matches must allow a newer, shorter prefix to replace an older one.
A single keyword gives a one-entry interval; ties may use any shortest valid interval.
